problems.description: A face lies on a closed (periodic) surface -- cylinder, torus, sphere, periodic B-spline -- and its boundary wraps around the periodic direction, but the file contains no seam edge. The wire closes in 3D yet is open in UV parameter space (e.g. two half-circles at top and bottom of a cylinder with nothing joining them along the U=0 isoline). OCCT detects the 2D-open wires, chooses a seam location, wraps the surface in a rectangular trimmed surface, and drives ShapeFix_ComposeShell to insert the seam and rebuild the face.

problems.description: A face on a surface with a parametric singularity (sphere pole, cone apex, degenerated torus apex, B-spline surface pinched to a point) is bounded by a wire that does not include the required degenerated (zero-3D-extent) edge at the singular row. Typically a single 'belt' wire wraps the surface once and the pole/apex boundary is simply absent. OCCT synthesizes a degenerated edge (B.Degenerated=true, 2D line pcurve along the singular isoline) and adds it as the second boundary, then proceeds with normal seam/bound processing.

problems.description: The wires of a face are wound the wrong way relative to the surface normal / to each other: the outer boundary is traversed clockwise (encloses the infinite point), a hole wire is oriented like an outer boundary, or outer and inner senses are swapped so that the material side is inverted. OCCT classifies each wire against the others (point-in-face tests anchored by PerformInfinitePoint) and reverses wires that disagree with the consensus.

problems.description: A face on a closed surface lacks its outer boundary: either the ADVANCED_FACE has no bounds at all (legal STEP for 'the whole surface'), or -- on a doubly-periodic surface (sphere, torus) -- it carries only hole wires, the intended semantics being 'entire surface minus holes'. OCCT creates the natural (full parametric rectangle) boundary: an empty face is rebuilt via BRepBuilderAPI_MakeFace; a holes-only face gets the natural bound added after shifting the holes by whole periods into the chosen fundamental domain.

problems.description: A face contains a wire that encloses (near-)zero area in UV -- a sliver loop, a collapsed rectangle of width ~1e-4, or a micro loop far below model tolerance. Such wires carry no usable material information and corrupt downstream classification. OCCT (ShapeAnalysis_Wire::CheckSmallArea inside ShapeFix_Face::FixSmallAreaWire) detects them and rebuilds the face without them; if every wire of the face is small the whole face can be removed from the model.

problems.description: A single wire actually contains more than one closed loop: a vertex is shared by more than two edges (graph degree > 2), e.g. a figure-eight EDGE_LOOP made of two triangles glued at one vertex, or an inner loop that touches the outer loop at a coincident vertex. Such a 'loop wire' is not a simple boundary. OCCT (CheckLoop + ShapeFix_Face::FixLoopWire) walks the edge graph from the high-degree vertices, extracts each closed sub-loop as its own wire, reorders closed loops, and stitches leftover open chains together by their common endpoints.

problems.description: A face (with at least two wires) contains a wire that consists of exactly two edges which are the same edge entity traversed twice -- a zero-area 'slit' loop that goes out along an edge and immediately back along the identical curve. The wire bounds no area and must be dropped. OCCT's FixWiresTwoCoincEdges rebuilds the face keeping every wire except those whose two edges are identical when both are oriented FORWARD.

problems.description: One face's wires actually bound several disjoint regions of the surface -- more than one closed wire acts as an 'outer' boundary (each possibly with its own holes), so the single FACE entity should really be several faces. This arises from merged faces on closed surfaces or from split-by-wire operations. OCCT's FixOrientation records which wires contain which (MapWires) and FixSplitFace then builds one face per outer wire, distributing hole wires by point-in-face classification and replacing the face with a compound.

problems.description: Within a single wire of a face, two non-adjacent edges intersect each other in the surface's UV space -- crossing diagonals (figure-eight written without a shared vertex), an edge passing through another edge's endpoint, or two edges lying collinearly on the same curve with overlapping ranges. OCCT's ShapeFix_IntersectionTool::FixSelfIntersectWire computes pairwise 2D intersections and heals by inserting a vertex at the crossing and splitting both edges, snapping to an existing nearby vertex (increasing its tolerance) when the crossing is near an edge end, merging endpoint vertices when both edges intersect at their ends, or cutting/splitting overlapped segments out of collinear edges.

problems.description: Two DIFFERENT wires of the same face intersect each other in UV: a hole boundary crosses the outer boundary, two hole wires cross, or wires share a collinear segment. Holes cut by intersecting wires make containment/orientation undecidable. OCCT's ShapeFix_IntersectionTool::FixIntersectingWires intersects all edge pairs across wire pairs and repairs exactly like the self-intersection case: vertex insertion + edge splitting at transverse crossings, vertex reuse near endpoints, vertex union at endpoint-endpoint contacts, and segment-overlap resolution (cutting edges back, 2-edge split for small overlaps, 3-edge reconstruction with a shared segment edge for large overlaps), then rebuilds the face from the modified wires.

problems.description: A seam edge on a closed surface carries two pcurves that are the same curve (or geometrically coincident) instead of two copies separated by the surface period -- e.g. a STEP SEAM_CURVE whose associated_geometry lists the same PCURVE twice. Both banks of the seam then map to one UV line and the face's UV domain collapses. OCCT detects the coincidence on reversed seam edges and translates the second pcurve by the U (or V) period.

problems.description: A wire consists solely of degenerated / zero-extent edges (all edges collapse to a single point, e.g. leftover pole caps or authoring debris): it bounds nothing and poisons seam construction and orientation analysis. OCCT removes such wires: FixMissingSeam drops completely-degenerated extra open wires before pairing seam wires; ComposeShell::DispatchWires prunes empty or single-degenerated-edge wires; FixOrientation quarantines near-null-length wires into VerySmallWires so they cannot corrupt classification.

problems.description: On a periodic surface, a face's wires are written with UV coordinates outside or straddling the canonical period window: one wire near u=0, another a full period away (u~2pi+x), or a wire wrapping across the seam so its 2D bounding box splits to opposite ends of the domain. Geometry is valid modulo the period, but naive containment/nesting tests see disjoint boxes and misclassify. OCCT normalizes with AdjustByPeriod/AdjustToPeriod: FixOrientation shifts wire boxes and probes wrapped copies (including diagonal +/-U x +/-V shifts on tori) and physically shifts pcurves (Shift2dWire); FixMissingSeam repositions the second wire by whole periods; FixAddNaturalBound shifts holes into the chosen fundamental domain.
